Under the Supreme Court Rules, 2025 (the “Supreme Court Rules”), two provisions in particular warrant attention for the purposes of the present matter: Order XX, Rule 2, and Order XXX, Part A, Rule 3. These provisions respectively govern (i) the procedure for seeking adjournment, and (ii) the consequences where adjournment is sought prosecuted without disruption caused by the absence, convenience, or scheduling preferences of individual counsel. The framework is put in place to ensure that proceedings before this Court are not stalled on grounds unconnected with any legal or unavoidable impediment. While this Court has shown and will continue to show indulgence where genuine exigencies are shown, such indulgence cannot be mistaken for acquiescence. Adjournments remain exceptions granted at the discretion of the Court, not entitlements. The persistent misuse of requests for adjournment, despite clear rules and warnings, is equivalent to 14. Moreover, unnecessary adjournments strike at the very heart of the access to justice. For litigants, particularly those of limited means, repeated adjournments translate into increased expense and, in effect, a denial of timely justice. This, in turn, erodes public confidence in the judicial system and runs contrary to the institutional efforts of this Court to ensure expeditious disposal of cases. It thus bears emphasis that the right to fair trial and due process under Article 10-A of the Constitution, as well as the larger constitutional promise of effective judicial remedies, cannot coexist with a culture of routine adjournments sought merely for impeding the duty, of this Court to fairly and effectively dispense justice, and shall be treated accordingly. adjournments sought without strict compliance with the legal framework and without demonstrable sufficient cause shall invite appropriate consequences, including imposition of compensatory costs in terms of the Supreme Court Rules. e / Islamabad, the 2nd of April, 2026 rtot approved for reporting
